articles.title: Tree vaccines and gene-edited butterflies among biotechnology projects funded by UK ‘invention agency’
articles.description: Exclusive: The tax-funded brainchild of Dominic Cummings hopes to find ways to speed up wild species’ evolution Vaccines for ash trees, skin treatments for newts and gene-edited swallowtail butterflies are among 14 tax-funded projects from the UK’s “invention agency” aiming to accelerate nature’s ability to adapt to the climate crisis. The £54m accelerated adaptation programme from the UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency (Aria) – a public body that funds high-risk, high-reward tech projects – aims to investigate applications of biotechnology that can speed up wild species’ evolution and help them to adapt to new threats such as global warming and disease. articles.description: As diet trends proliferate on social media, it can be hard to work out which are backed by science and which should be ignored. From paleo to keto, raw food to intermittent fasting, each attracts a tribe of ardent followers. Now Daniel Lieberman, professor of biological sciences at Harvard University, has written a book to try to cut through the noise. In Fed Up, he uses his background as an evolutionary anthropologist to scrutinise the evidence, turning himself into a guinea pig in the process and trying various diets. In this podcast, he tells Ian Sample which one has remained part of his routine Order Fed Up from the Guardian Bookshop Support the Guardian: theguardian.com/sciencepod Continue reading...

articles.title: US judge declines to block transfer of wildlife refuge land to Musk’s SpaceX
articles.description: Environmental groups vow to continue opposition to deal that would expand site for Elon Musk rocket company A federal judge on Monday refused to block the Trump administration from giving SpaceX more than 700 acres of wildlife refuge as part of a land swap in Texas, while environmental groups vowed to continue their legal challenge. US district judge Fernando Rodriguez Jr declined the plaintiffs’ request for a preliminary injunction to prevent the parcel exchange, saying they failed to prove it would worsen ecological risks to a Gulf coast region already transformed by billionaire Elon Musk’s rocket operations. Continue reading...

articles.title: Discovery of new Australian stick insect species reveals case of mistaken identity
articles.description: New study describes two species, Anchiale robusta and Anchiale mabiensis, both found in far north Queensland Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here Two new large stick insect species have been identified by Australian researchers, in a discovery they say illustrates how little we still understand about insect diversity. The two species, both found in far north Queensland, are described in a study published in Austral Entomology. Sign up for climate and environment editor Adam Morton’s free Clear Air newsletter here Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Jaw-dropping’ El Niño bursts through temperature record months before peak
articles.description: ‘Godzilla-level’ phenomenon is supercharging the climate crisis and will have a huge impact on communities across the world The “jaw-dropping” El Niño currently heating up the planet has burst through the highest temperature ever recorded for the phenomenon, several months before its expected peak. The latest data shows the temperature rise at the heart of El Niño in the Pacific Ocean has now reached 3.05C. That is higher than the 3.02C set in late November 2015, the previous high set in the 150 years of modern records. This temperature is measured against the average of 1991-2020. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Planetary boundaries’ necessary for flourishing of life have been massively breached, scientists warn
articles.description: New report shows key indicators of Earth’s health are ‘outside the safe operating space’ as climate disaster looms The planetary life support systems relied upon by humans have deteriorated to their worst levels ever recorded amid ongoing pollution and habitat destruction, according to a key yet grim annual update by scientists. Of the nine “planetary boundaries” that help determine whether life can flourish on Earth, seven are being breached at their highest ever levels of transgression, according to the latest planetary health check, a process that was established in 2009. Continue reading...

articles.title: Baby girls’ greater interest in faces offers clue to nature v nurture debate
articles.description: Study finds overall differences between groups of newborns by sex that are likely to be determined by biology The question dates back to the first man and woman: how does the world shape the behaviour of the sexes, and what differences, if any, are present at birth? Untangling the contributions of nature versus nurture has proved challenging for scientists, and controversial at times, but a new study of babies sheds light on at least one aspect of the puzzle. Continue reading...

articles.title: Trump reportedly to form health funding board that could veto ‘woke’ initiatives
articles.description: President’s latest order expected to bring NIH funding under control of Trump administration to align with agenda Donald Trump’s latest executive order is expected to establish a board responsible for approving National Institutes of Health (NIH) grant funding, marking another attempt by the Trump administration to censor topics that do not align with the president’s agenda. The executive order, reported by outlets including the Washington Post and Politico, was discussed in a meeting on Friday in which senior administration officials accused the NIH of funding “woke” initiatives that went against Trump’s political priorities. Continue reading...

articles.title: Tree vaccines and gene-edited butterflies among biotechnology projects funded by UK ‘invention agency’
articles.description: Exclusive: The tax-funded brainchild of Dominic Cummings hopes to find ways to speed up wild species’ evolution Vaccines for ash trees, skin treatments for newts and gene-edited swallowtail butterflies are among 14 tax-funded projects from the UK’s “invention agency” aiming to accelerate nature’s ability to adapt to the climate crisis. The £54m accelerated adaptation programme from the UK’s Advanced Research and Invention Agency (Aria) – a public body that funds high-risk, high-reward tech projects – aims to investigate applications of biotechnology that can speed up wild species’ evolution and help them to adapt to new threats such as global warming and disease. Continue reading...

articles.title: Who will start for England at Euro 2028? BBC Sport's predictions
articles.description: As England prepare to face world champions Spain on Saturday, BBC Sport's experts predict who will be starting for the Three Lions at Euro 2028.

articles.title: Cyclist who dressed as man to avoid Taliban wins silver medal
articles.description: Afghan cyclist Fariba Hashimi wins silver in the women's road race at the Asian Games, having fled oppression in her home country to pursue a sporting dream.

articles.title: Menzies upsets Van Veen to win second title of year
articles.description: Scotland's Cameron Menzies celebrates his second tournament win of the year after beating Gian van Veen to the Players Championship 29 title in Den Bosch.

articles.title: Keothavong 'can't fault' GB after BJK Cup loss to Czechs
articles.description: Sonay Kartal and Katie Boulter lose their singles matches as Great Britain are beaten by a strong Czech Republic side in the Billie Jean King Cup quarter-finals.

articles.title: Will a switch to light speed cut power use at data centres?
articles.description: To save power and add capacity, data centres are switching from copper wires to tech using light.

articles.title: A new skyline of data centres is rising from the rolling plains of rural China
articles.description: Potato farmers rub shoulders with rows of gleaming new data centres as Trump and Xi meet to discuss AI safety.

articles.title: Rare look at the remote engine rooms powering China's AI ambitions
articles.description: The BBC is in Inner Mongolia where dozen of Chinese data centres are being constructed, as the country aims to lead the world in artificial intelligence.

articles.title: Call of Duty's Activision to make next Halo game as Xbox cuts more jobs
articles.description: The news comes as part of a "reset" announced by Xbox in July, with 3,600 planned job losses overall.

articles.title: Not all AI workers think the tech could kill everyone
articles.description: In text exchanges and conversations, multiple people who have worked for leading companies are sceptical of the warnings.

articles.title: Google's Gemini AI hacked three companies in security test
articles.description: The AI model accessed the internet and guessed credentials to three websites, a Google official told the BBC.

articles.title: Would Australians support a smart glasses ban?
articles.description: As Australia considers barring the use of smart glasses in government offices, the BBC asks people in Sydney what they think.

articles.title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained
articles.description: Training systems that allow robots to negotiate the real world are getting more sophisticated.
